issues.description: The script uses XMLHttpRequest to fetch external scripts and executes them via a[a][a](x.responseText), which is equivalent to eval(). This allows remote code execution from arbitrary URLs.
issues.recommendation: Remove dynamic code execution and only use static, trusted code. Avoid eval or similar constructs.

issues.description: The script executes code using a[a][a](x.responseText), which is an obfuscated way to call the Function constructor (i.e., window['constructor']['constructor'] = Function). This is a strong sign of code obfuscation.
issues.recommendation: Avoid obfuscation and use clear, readable code. Remove dynamic code execution.

issues.description: The script loads third-party libraries via @require from GreasyFork and CDN (jQuery). The GreasyFork scripts are not version-pinned with hashes, and the CDN could be updated or compromised.
issues.recommendation: Pin dependencies to specific versions and use trusted, official sources. Prefer SRI hashes if possible.

issues.description: The script requests a large set of @grant permissions, including unsafeWindow and GM_getTabs/GM_saveTab, which are not all used in the visible code. This increases the attack surface.
issues.recommendation: Request only the minimum permissions required for functionality.

issues.description: The script manipulates innerHTML/outerHTML and document structure in various places (e.g., deleteElement, watchAndDelete), and the code is designed to run on hundreds of sites, increasing the risk of DOM-based XSS if user input is ever inserted.
issues.location: Utils.deleteElement, watchAndDelete, and general script structure
issues.recommendation: Sanitize all user input and avoid inserting untrusted data into the DOM.

issues.description: The script stores a unique user identifier (UUID) in GM storage and increments a counter. While not directly exfiltrated, this is a form of persistent user tracking.
issues.recommendation: Disclose tracking clearly and avoid persistent identifiers unless necessary.

issues.description: The script's @antifeature explicitly states 'Tracking, for performance debugging', indicating intentional user tracking.
issues.recommendation: Make tracking opt-in and provide clear privacy disclosures.
